links.targetTitle: On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital is deliberately not equival

title: Final penalty determination reconciles the automated ledger against the verified record and can revise it in either direction
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.3.3 enumerates three outcomes when the interim OVRC penalty ledger meets "the definitive TRC history, which incorporates all validated information from the TRC Report including any intra-period shortfalls."

If the real shortfall was worse than or invisible to OVRC, existing accruals "will be adjusted upwards to match the actual shortfall"; if OVRC detected nothing, "penalties will be assessed and applied retroactively based on the full duration and magnitude of the actual shortfall." If the two agree, accruals "will be confirmed and finalized." And if TRC was in fact higher than "a misleading OVRC reading" that produced an erroneous penalty, "Core GovOps will adjust or void the penalty accordingly."

Symmetry is what makes the scheme legitimate. A ledger that could only be revised upward would be a one-way ratchet on a signal known to be imperfect, and Primes would rationally over-collateralise against measurement noise rather than against risk. Voidability makes the automated ledger a provisional estimate rather than a verdict.

Retroactive assessment is the other half: it removes the incentive to structure a shortfall so that on-chain monitoring cannot see it. Evading the automated detector delays the charge rather than avoiding it, which is precisely what makes the off-chain disclosure obligation enforceable — the disclosure and the penalty are wired to the same determination.

A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3.1 places this reconciliation inside "the monthly settlement cycles," so the correction has a fixed cadence rather than being open-ended.
description: Core GovOps adjusts accruals upward or applies them retroactively where OVRC missed or understated a shortfall, confirms them where they match, and voids them where a misleading reading created one.
